assessment.nobel_worthiness: Brought electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal policy into formal and empirical economics. It created a coherent research programme, now standard in political economics, and has shaped work on development and public finance. Broad influence across fields and high policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini built the main theoretical and empirical framework on constitutions and policy outcomes. Besley and Persson developed the state capacity and development strand. A three-person grouping is defensible, but the credit split between the two overlapping pairs is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Core work dates from the 1990s and 2000s and has been tested and extended for two decades. It is mature enough to recognise now.
uncertainties: Some constitutional-effects estimates face identification challenges, since constitutions are not randomly assigned.
Whether the committee prefers the Persson-Tabellini pairing or the broader three-person grouping.
Other political-economy contributors (e.g. Acemoglu, Robinson) are outside this ballot item, and I did not assess them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy models of trade protection (the 'Protection for Sale' framework) and their work on trade, innovation and growth are foundational. They gave the field a micro-founded account of why trade policy departs from free trade, and the work remains central to teaching and research.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are the clear joint originators of the lobbying-and-protection framework and of the endogenous-growth-in-open-economies work. Credit is cleanly shared between the two. Helpman also appears on the heterogeneous-firm item, which strengthens the case for him specifically.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1980s to the 1990s and has been widely confirmed and used. Timing risk comes from being a long-standing candidate, not from lack of maturity.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale equation is mixed, and structural estimates vary.
Competition from the firm-heterogeneity trade strand, where Helpman is also credited.
Theory-heavy contribution; the committee may weigh policy impact differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Changed the understanding of how technology and trade shocks reshape local labour markets and wage inequality. The China-shock evidence showed large, persistent adjustment costs, and the task-based framework restructured labour demand analysis. This is clean, design-based evidence on a first-order policy question. Close to my own field, but I judge it on the common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Hanson are central to the empirical trade-shock and labour-market adjustment results. Dorn is an important co-author. Katz's skill-biased change work overlaps with prior recognised work (Goldin). The task framework also has important co-originators outside this credited set, which complicates the attribution.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from 2013 to 2016, with a decade of follow-up. The results are widely replicated, though debates continue on magnitudes and mechanisms.
uncertainties: Debate over exposure measures, shift-share identification validity and long-run persistence.
Interpretation of the decline in manufacturing relative to automation, and the exact share attributable to trade.
Two-person versus larger grouping, and the overlap with the task-based literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints that amplify and propagate shocks (credit cycles) are a foundational mechanism in macroeconomics and were central to understanding the 2008 crisis. The framework is the workhorse of modern macro-finance models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 'Credit Cycles' is the clear originating paper. Gertler and Gilchrist represent the closely related financial-accelerator line, but the primary credit belongs to Kiyotaki and Moore. Gertler also appears on the New Keynesian item.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of use, extension and policy application, including after the 2008 crisis. Highly mature.
uncertainties: Boundary with the Bernanke-Gertler financial accelerator, whose co-originators are not all on this ballot item (Bernanke has already been recognised).
Empirical identification of collateral channels is mostly indirect.
Some of the benefit of this work may be seen as already recognised through the 2022 financial-crisis prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are among the most widely used tools in applied economics, especially in labour, industrial organisation, growth and finance. The contribution is mainly methodological, but its impact on empirical practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991), Arellano-Bover (1995) and Blundell-Bond (1998) form a clear lineage, so the credited trio is reasonably well defined. Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen, and Anderson-Hsiao, are important antecedents not on this item.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use; well-understood limitations (weak and many instruments) are documented and the tools are standard.
uncertainties: Known problems of instrument proliferation and weak identification limit how far the methods can be trusted in practice.
Econometric-methods prizes usually require broad conceptual novelty beyond a widely used estimator.
Credit for the antecedents.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression allows analysis of the whole conditional distribution, not just means, and is used in labour, inequality, finance and risk work. The idea is simple and general, and the practical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker developed the theory and software. Chernozhukov's contribution is mainly in later inference, instrumental-variable and distributional extensions, and he is also on the ML causal item. The core credit is with the first two.
assessment.maturity: Almost five decades of use, with a mature theory and a long record of applications.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently transformative compared with other econometric contributions.
Whether to include Chernozhukov, who is credited for later work and also appears on another ballot item.
Statistical origins partly lie in earlier work outside economics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins modern monetary-policy analysis in central banks. Taylor's rule and Woodford's and Gali's theoretical synthesis have shaped practice and teaching. Its policy influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. The framework was developed by many people (Calvo, Taylor, Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans, Smets-Wouters, Gertler, Woodford, Gali, and others) over decades, and a three-person cap leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of use. Debates after the 2008 crisis and the 2021-22 inflation episode have raised questions about parts of the framework.
uncertainties: Large and diffuse set of contributors makes a clean three-person selection difficult.
Recent inflation experience and the rise of heterogeneous-agent models may affect how the committee assesses the framework.
The empirical evidence for the specific Phillips curve is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data brought a new level of credibility and detail to measurement of intergenerational mobility and neighbourhood effects. The work has had major influence on public debate and on policy design. It sits in the register-based tradition I know from Nordic work, but it is judged here on the common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the programme, with Hendren central to the neighbourhood-effects and mobility-by-place work. Friedman and Katz are important co-authors. Nordic and other register studies of mobility (and the earlier theory of mobility) are also relevant antecedents.
assessment.maturity: Key papers date from 2014 to 2022, so it is less mature than other candidates. Long-run replication across countries is still developing and some results on causal neighbourhood effects are recent.
uncertainties: Relatively recent; the committee may prefer more time for confirmation.
Causal interpretation of place effects and of rank-rank mobility statistics remains debated.
Chetty also appears on the tax item, and credit among the four named is uncertain.
